newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-SYMONDS OPTS FOR AUSTRALIA NOT ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SYMONDS OPTS FOR AUSTRALIA NOT ENGLAND.

text.p: English-born batsman Andrew Symonds on Wednesday opted to play for Australia and not England in a decision that places his county championship career with Gloucestershire in jeopardy.
Symonds, who was eligible for either country after being raised in Australia, said he will play for Australia A in a limited overs match against West Indies in Melbourne on Friday.
"I'm an Aussie and always have been and I will play my cricket for Australia. I will play on Friday," Symonds told reporters at a news conference to announce his plans.
His decision to turn his back on England almost certainly means the end of his Gloucestershire career.
Symonds, who refused a place in the England A side to tour Pakistan last year, will now be considered an overseas player under county championship rules.
Each county is allowed to sign one overseas player and Gloucestershire have West Indies captain and fast bowler Courtney Walsh under contract for 1997.
Gloucestershire chief executive Philip August on Monday said Walsh is club captain, adding: "So we couldn't really dump him".
Symonds' contract with Gloucestershire stipulated that he would be available for England, if selected.
After rejecting his England A tour place, Symonds returned to Queensland during the southern hemisphere summer to play Sheffield Shield cricket.
England selector David Graveney, who is manager of the current England A tour in Australia, said he was pleased Symonds' position has been settled.
"This has clarified the situation and is probably a great relief for him," Graveney told reporters in Brisbane.
